newsitem.title: INDIA: CRICKET-MARSH ACCUSES SIDE OF LACK OF PROFESSIONALISM.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-MARSH ACCUSES SIDE OF LACK OF PROFESSIONALISM.

text.p: Australian coach Geoff Marsh has accused his side of lacking professionalism following their seven wicket defeat to India on Sunday.
The unofficial world champions were outplayed on a spinner's pitch, losing the one-off match by seven wickets with a day to spare.
"They have trained a little like millionaires instead of getting down to business," Marsh said. "Some of these guys have been very casual.
"The boys have got to tighten up on their professionalism. You can look for all the excuses in the world why we didn't play well but these guys are professional sportsmen.
"The way they got themselves out on the first day when the wicket was pretty good was disappointing.
"If we'd applied ourselves to make a test 100, which is made in over five hours by all great test cricketers, we would have made a lot more runs.
"We only needed another 100 runs in the first innings but our batting never changed in the second innings."
India will meet South Africa in a three-test series, the first between the two countries in India, following a triangular one-day series which will also involve Australia.
"India is always tough country to beat in India," said South African captain Hansie Cronje on arrival in Bombay on Monday. "Even then we rate our chances 50-50."
South Africa will be weakened by the absence of all-rounders Craig Matthews and Jacques Kallis, fast bowler Shaun Pollock and left-arm wrist spinner Paul Adams.

"No doubt we will miss them, but we have very good replacements for them," Cronje said. "The newcomers had their workout in the recent four-nation tournament in Kenya, which we won, and I am sure they will do well here."
Coach Bob Woolmer, who toured India with Tony Greig's successful England side in 1975-76, said there were some exciting prospects in the South African side.

"Derek Crookes is a promising batsman and off-spinner. Nicy Boje is a left-arm spinner and an outstanding fielder, both close in and in the deep," he said. "Lance Klusener is a left-handed batsman and a right-arm medium pacer. Herschelle Gibbs is a stylish batsman."
Woolmer also confirmed the South Africans had done their homework on their opponents.
"Anil Kumble is already known as a world-class bowler, even though I have not seen him. I have also heard of newcomer, spinner Sunil Joshi. So let us see," Woolmer said.
"All in all, we have come fully prepared."
